properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued July 31 at 11:21AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
At 1121 AM CDT...Fair weather waterspouts were located along a line
extending from 14 nm southwest of Farewell Buoy to 24 nm south of
Gulf Shores Beach...moving southeast at 10 knots.

These waterspouts will remain over mainly open waters.

The primary threats from these waterspouts are wind gusts up to 30
knots and locally higher waves. Boaters should consider seeking safe
harbor until these waterspouts have passed.

Weather conditions support the development of waterspouts.
Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous
waves and seas. If a waterspout is sighted...seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.area: Coastal waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS out 20 NM; Waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued July 31 at 11:43AM EDT until July 31 at 1:15PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 115 PM EDT.

* At 1143 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 26 nm
northwest of Suwannee River to 33 nm south of Buckeye Reef, moving
southeast at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Horseshoe Beach and Suwannee River.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.
properties.area: Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM; Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued July 31 at 11:24AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
At 1124 AM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Steinhatchee, moving southeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Cross City, Steinhatchee, Horseshoe Point, Suwannee, Horseshoe Beach,
Tennille, Fish Creek, Shamrock, Howell Place, Clara, Shired Island,
Cross City Airport, Old Town, Jena, Hines, Jonesboro, Bird Island,
Eugene, Yellow Jacket, and Fanning Springs.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.
properties.area: Inland Taylor; Inland Dixie; Coastal Taylor; Coastal Dixie

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 31 at 9:57AM CDT until July 31 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Saint Clair County in southwestern Illinois...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 957 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Belleville, O'Fallon, East St. Louis, Collinsville, Fairview
Heights, Cahokia, Swansea, Shiloh, Centreville, Freeburg,
Caseyville, Washington Park, Dupo, Millstadt, Madison, Cahokia
Parks Airport, Smithton and Fairmont City.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 9:10AM CDT until August 1 at 2:00PM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Aberdeen has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in South Dakota...

Little Minnesota River near Peever affecting Roberts County.

.For sites with a river forecast, the forecast includes precipitation
through the next 24 hours. Any future precipitation could affect the
forecasts.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Little Minnesota River near Peever.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Left bank below gage begins flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 AM CDT Friday the stage was 16.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 17.2 feet this afternoon. It will then
fall below flood stage by early this evening.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abr.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 830 PM CDT.

stop, turn around and go another way.

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued July 27 at 10:40AM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10:00 AM PDT Friday July 31.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
